item.title: Haunted Histories Of Faith And Dalit Christian Women’s Voices In Malayalam Literature
item.description: From the spectral testimony of Rosykutty to the everyday defiance of schoolgirls, these texts challenge the histories produced by upper-caste Kerala literature, which frequently marginalises or silences Dalit experiences. The post Haunted Histories Of Faith And Dalit Christian Women’s Voices In Malayalam Literature appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Why We Fell In Love With Heated Rivalry’s Shane And Ilya
item.description: Heated Rivalry explores how queer men are forced to navigate the patriarchy and gendered norms and make choices that no one should have to make, such as deciding between a successful career and being with their partner in public. The post Why We Fell In Love With Heated Rivalry’s Shane And Ilya appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Whose Bodies To Protect, Whose To Surveil: Akootai And Sexual Health Politics In Colonial India
item.description: Today, the so-called ‘old, ugly, broken down’ Indian sex worker of British India emerges as a subaltern figure in need of historical reinvestigation. Women’s History Month invites us to delve into those histories that remain obfuscated or partially explored. The post Whose Bodies To Protect, Whose To Surveil: Akootai And Sexual Health Politics In Colonial India appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Israel-Iran War And Local Consequences: Kashmir Under Restrictions Again
item.description: The closure of Lal Chowk’s Ghanta Ghar during peaceful mourning gatherings drew political reaction. The post Israel-Iran War And Local Consequences: Kashmir Under Restrictions Again appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Manikuntala Sen: Building A Women’s Movement Within The Indian Left | #IndianWomenInHistory
item.description: Manikuntala Sen’s work offers invaluable insight into the making of a women’s movement and the everyday challenges and dilemmas faced by an activist. The post Manikuntala Sen: Building A Women’s Movement Within The Indian Left | #IndianWomenInHistory appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: The Women History Forgot: Kulin Wives, Widows, And Sex Workers
item.description: It becomes the job of feminist historiographers to attempt reconstruction of the lifeworlds of women history forgot, so that we may be able to imagine their existence beyond a lens of historical victimhood. The post The Women History Forgot: Kulin Wives, Widows, And Sex Workers appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Sarala Ray: The Tumultuous Path to Stree Shiksha | #IndianWomenInHistory
item.description: Sarala Ray remains an unignorable name in the discourse of Stree Shiksha, especially in Bengal, and the school she established stands to date as one of the most sought-after institutions of knowledge in present-day Kolkata. The post Sarala Ray: The Tumultuous Path to Stree Shiksha | #IndianWomenInHistory appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Negotiating Autonomy And The Idea Of ‘Permitted Freedom’ In One’s Own Home
item.description: Sociologists believe that women don’t just surrender to certain adjustments; they perpetually recalibrate their behaviour in different scenarios. They know that the autonomy that is unchallenged in the city must be exerted carefully back home. The post Negotiating Autonomy And The Idea Of ‘Permitted Freedom’ In One’s Own Home appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: The Politics Of Respectability: Who Is Allowed To Look “Put Together”?
item.description: Who is complimented for appearing well-groomed and who is criticized shows how gender, caste, or class discrimination work. The post The Politics Of Respectability: Who Is Allowed To Look “Put Together”? appeared first on Feminism in India.
